method: Force-corrected NEBB (non-equilibrium bounce-back) wall boundary condition with Guo/EDM body-force driver for D2Q9/D3Q19 LBM Poiseuille channel flow
oss_reference: haimingz/vivsim (JAX, Apache-2.0): lbm/boundary/nebb.py, lbm/boundary/_helpers.py, lbm/forcing/{edm,guo}.py, lbm/basic.py, examples/2d/poiseuille_channel.py
literature: Guo, Z., Zheng, C., & Shi, B. (2002). Discrete lattice effects on the forcing term in the lattice Boltzmann method. Phys. Rev. E, 65, 046308.
Zou, Q., & He, X. (1997). On pressure and velocity boundary conditions for the lattice Boltzmann method. Phys. Fluids, 9(6), 2315-2324.
Batchelor, G. K. (1967). An Introduction to Fluid Dynamics, §4.2 (Poiseuille flow).
Ladd, A. J. C. (1994). Numerical simulations of particulate suspensions via a discretized Boltzmann equation. J. Fluid Mech., 271, 285-309.
migration_plan: Already implemented in TensorLBM. Two arms: (A) D2Q9 NEBB module (tensorlbm.nebb_bodyforce.BodyForceChannel) with force-corrected wall velocity u_wall - F/(2ρ) and shear-reconstruction NEBB kernel; (B) D3Q19 main solver (GPUCorePathSolver) with collide_guo_into + apply_channel_walls (half-way bounce-back). Both validated against closed-form Poiseuille solution.
validation_status: PASS (D2Q9: 6e-14 machine precision; D3Q19: 0.31% at ny=10, 0.12% at ny=20; both < 3% ecosystem stretch and < 15% owner threshold)

key_formulas.nebb_shear_reconstruction: f_k = f_k^eq(ρ_w, u_w_corrected) - f_opp^eq(ρ_w, u_w_corrected) + f_opp
